plan_a_advantages: More targeted intensity work (tempo run and hill workouts) to improve speed.
Longer runs with moderate elevation to simulate trail conditions and build endurance.
A more balanced approach to volume and intensity, avoiding excessive easy running.
plan_b_advantages: Simpler and more concise, potentially easier to adhere to.
Includes a strength and mobility session, which is beneficial for injury prevention and overall fitness.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a more strategic blend of volume and intensity, including longer runs at moderate elevation and dedicated tempo work to build lactate threshold – crucial for faster trail running. Plan B, while focusing on aerobic base building, lacks sufficient intensity and elevation gain, which are key drivers of speed in trail running. Plan A’s inclusion of hill workouts and a longer, sustained effort run directly addresses the demands of the terrain and the goal of improved speed.
